A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVLM-VA research. Their complete main texts and supplementary material are readable, including equations, figures, tables and prompts. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DecoyMNIST, skin-lesion and knee-radiograph experiments, including alignment results, baseline comparisons and component analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a user study, quantitative cluster-count sensitivity results and tests of robustness to global image corruptions.

M1.justification: Low-entropy sampling, PPEPS-WGM segmentation, Critic/Judge mask generation and RRR fine-tuning remain unchanged. The appendix prompts and training procedure are retained. The revised alignment metric concerns evaluation rather than the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The three image datasets remain, but v2 substantially extends evaluation to human judgments through an 18-participant study on both medical datasets. Appendix A.5 also introduces globally corrupted skin-image scenarios using gamma correction, focus blur and contrast changes, extending coverage beyond localized confounders.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DFR, JTT, SUBG, the original model, ground-truth-mask alignment and SAM segmentation. GPT-5, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama4 and Qwen3 already appear in v1, including its appendix; they are not newly added comparators.

E3.justification: v2 redefines the DecoyMNIST alignment metric using per-image normalized absolute attribution. It also introduces a 26-question human-evaluation protocol, quantitative cluster-count testing and clean-versus-corrupted accuracy-drop comparisons. These substantially expand evaluation design without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. v2's added statement that test decoys are absent conflicts with its retained random-decoy description, so an actual decoy-removal change is not established.

E4.justification: Section 6 adds direct human assessments of cluster relevance, Critic reasoning and explanation alignment. Appendix A.2 supplements the existing qualitative cluster illustration with quantitative sensitivity results, while A.5 adds global-corruption robustness tests. The embedding analysis is relocated from the main text, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seven seeds, mean ± standard deviation reporting and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests at p < 0.05. The new corruption analysis uses the same statistical practice. The user study reports percentages without introducing uncertainty estimates or significance procedures.

E6.justification: New findings include 88% cluster agreement, 87% reasoning agreement and 86% preference for aligned explanations; verdict accuracies of 0.68/0.84/0.86/0.86 for J = 3/5/7/9; and reductions in corruption-induced accuracy loss of 0.025/0.022/0.055 for gamma correction/focus blur/contrast. These substantially expand reported evidence. Existing medical benchmark scores and previous LVLM/SAM comparison results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The alignment metric's mathematical definition changes substantively: v1 subtracts pooled signed attribution within spurious masks divided by total mask area; v2 subtracts the average per-image fraction of absolute attribution within those masks. This is a limited definition revision. The PPEPS-WGM derivation and RRR objective remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: bidirectional translation between explanations and human specifications, PPEPS-WGM segmentation, and reduced shortcut dependence without fine-grained feedback. The new experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the explicit caveat about context-dependent spuriousness with a spatial-separability limitation. Appendix A.5 explains why suppressing attribution in irrelevant regions might improve robustness even when global shortcuts cannot be isolated. New interpretations also connect participant agreement to human alignment and cluster-count results to hyperparameter robustness.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly provides a code-repository link, and Table 1 dates its LVLM cost estimates to November 2025. The supplied PDFs do not establish repository accessibility. Existing hardware, software, training hyperparameters, data counts and prompt specifications are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kuhn et al. on VLM-based shortcut mitigation in transformers and Di Salvo et al. on MedMNIST-C. These provide limited positioning and experimental context. Most cited works remain unchanged; publication metadata updates do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 introduces numbered sections and lettered supplementary sections, changes citation style and author-affiliation formatting, and makes localized prose edits. The embedding discussion moves to Appendix A.4. The main narrative order and most existing prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the cluster-count results table and moves v1 Figure 5's embedding visualization to supplementary Figure 11. The alignment-versus-lambda plot becomes Figure 5 with a wider aspect ratio and reorganized legend. Typography, captions and page flow change, while the remaining scientific graphics and existing table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The user study and new sensitivity and corruption analyses strengthen evidence for human alignment and robustness. The normalized alignment definition and code-access link also improve the paper. These gains are limited by sparse reporting of the new studies, the unexplained relationship between the revised metric and retained alignment curve, and the newly contradictory test-decoy description. Overall, v2 provides useful additional validation without fundamentally changing the method or established benchmark evidence.
